(A) STYLE-OBJECT ASSERTIONS THAT PROVE NOTHING. Defects 1 and 3 were both real, correct declarations in the flattened style object -- exactly what the RNTL tests assert via StyleSheet.flatten() -- that the platform then ignored or overrode at render time. A test asserting `flatten(style).gap === 8` passes while the DOM shows no gap; a test asserting minHeight:44 passes while the visible control is the wrong size. This pattern is used widely across the repo (it predates 008 -- see 004's and 006's tests too), so the fix is a repo-wide testing-methodology decision, not a one-file change. Decide what replaces it (render-structure assertions, a real layout-measuring approach, snapshot-of-structure, or something else), write it down in docs/verification.md as a rule with the reasoning, and convert the existing assertions of this shape. (B) CROSS-PLATFORM DIVERGENCE NOTHING CHECKS. Defect 5 is the clean example: native and web disagreed about the active-tab color and no test, type, or review round could see it, because each platform's file was individually correct. Anywhere .ios/.android/.web variants or platform defaults can drift (tint colors, safe-area handling, inline-vs-flex element semantics, font fallbacks), there is currently no mechanism that notices.
